skill: Applying statistical and analytical tools and techniques
expected_level_description: You can: - support the development of statistical and analytical insights and reports under supervision - explain the benefits of basic statistical and analytical techniques - explain the value of quality assurance and best practices in developing statistical and analytical outputs

skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - explain why it's important to communicate technical concepts in non-technical language - explain the types of communication that can be used with internal and external stakeholders, and their impact
You can: - explain the importance of using data ethics and privacy in your work - identify appropriate channels to discuss ethical issues, with support
You can: - explain the importance of data governance policies - explain how data management tools, procedures and methods relate to a specific project

You can: - explain the importance of data models and their uses - identify appropriate channels in your organisation to learn about data modelling and quality standards - identify data quality issues and provide possible solutions to resolve them - prepare and cleanse data under supervision, contributing to making it fit for purpose

You can: - develop and use an appropriate data visualisation under supervision to tell a meaningful story that is relevant to set goals - explain the value of sharing a story effectively - explain why it's important to develop inclusive, accessible data visualisations that recognise different user needs

You can: - explain why it's important to understand the organisation's priorities - contribute to the development of data products to deliver business impact - explain how to align data and analysis to meet business requirements

You can: - explain the importance of coding for analysis - explain the value of maintaining analytical approach documentation - design an analytical approach with support, for example, writing simple code

You can: - understand a problem statement and explain the intended outcome of a data project - explain the importance of data in solving a problem - explain why it's important to adapt your ways of working to deliver different project outcomes and requirements
You can: - describe the main parts of the health and care system and the services the organisation supports - explain why patient safety and confidentiality matter in your work
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - run data quality checks and correct errors - explain data quality reports to colleagues
You can: - explain the difference between identifiable, pseudonymised, and anonymised data - follow the organisation's rules for suppressing small numbers in outputs
You can: - explain the difference between a clinical terminology and a classification - recognise common terminologies such as SNOMED CT and ICD
